gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Bold, cut-open lettering: Gugi lets its lowercase nearly match the capitals in height. And Noto Sans Old Turkic, a sans-serif with chunky forms and wide mouths, takes over once the display voice has said its piece.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Rounded-rod lettering, bold and distinctive: Gugi draws every curve and stem in a single weight, with terminals cut open. Noto Sans Oriya, a sans with generous curve gaps, reads smoothly across paragraphs.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Gugi draws bold, single-weight letters whose lowercase nearly reaches the capitals. Noto Sans Palmyrene is the quieter half, a sans whose curves stop short and whose ascenders stay compressed, so the display voice stands out.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Gugi keeps its line free of any brush-style swell, drawing bold letters with cut-open terminals and lowercase near capital height. Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau reads gently, open-ended curves giving lines room.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Noto Sans PhagsPa feels approachable, a sans with see-through c openings and only a gentle bump from small letters up to capitals. Gugi belongs big and brief, where its single-width line can show.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Gugi sets down bold, constant-width lines with its lowercase climbing nearly to the capitals. Noto Sans Phoenician lets its s curves open wide at both ends, giving that heading a modern, generous partner.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahlavi: Distinctive from the first glance, Gugi gives its o a ring with a constant wall. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi is the approachable counterweight, its e mouths gaping and its capitals barely rising.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Bold, plainly drawn: Gugi looks made with a single pen tip. Gugi belongs where it is large and brief, while Noto Sans Sunuwar, a sans-serif whose curves leave daylight, handles everything else.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Wire-smooth and bold, Gugi glides under the eye, with cut-open terminals and lowercase rising nearly to capital height. Gugi makes statements; Noto Sans Syloti Nagri, a sans-serif, explains them.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-syriac-western: Gugi draws bold letters with no thick-thin flicker anywhere. Give Noto Sans Syriac Western, a sans with sturdy small letters and terminals held far from the stroke, a little extra size.
